defects_fixed: 117.43-01 ArtifactComparison.isWellFormed compared only artifact NAME SETS and never hash VALUES, so a bitIdentical claim contradicted by differing SHA-256 digests was accepted and the shipped 113.39 gate returned pass on a false identity claim; proven before the fix (aaa.../bbb... reported isWellFormed == true). Fix compares recorded values.

117.43-03 shipped in commit 186c05a but undocumented until 2026-10-03: measureChecksums walked only one direction - a signed artifact with no checksum line was reported as uncovered, but a checksum LINE naming an unreadable artifact was never counted, so an inventory could name artifacts the tree does not contain and still report clean agreement. Now counted as phantom and fails closed.

117.43-04 shipped in commit 186c05a but undocumented until 2026-10-03: readChecksumIndex documented that it returns the map 'plus every line that was malformed, so a silently dropped line cannot shrink the covered set without being counted', but returned the map alone and continued past malformed input, so a truncated or uppercase digest vanished from the inventory with no counted failure. Now returns ChecksumIndex(index, malformed) and malformed lines fail the check.

117.43-05 found and fixed in this slice (2026-10-03): readChecksumIndex filled its map with `index[path] = digest`, so a path recorded TWICE with DIFFERENT digests kept whichever line came last and the contradicting claim was counted nowhere - an inventory that disagreed with itself reported agreement on the surviving line. ChecksumIndex now carries `conflicting` (repeated paths whose digests disagree) as a measured result rather than an internal detail, and measureChecksums counts it as its own violation (conflicting=<n> in observed, conflicting: <path> in note). Same fail-open shape as 117.43-04 one step lower: there the line vanished from the inventory, here it overwrote its own evidence. Identical repeats stay benign and are tested explicitly. Fix does not change any committed checksum value and does not touch build/.

117.43-06 ArtifactComparison.isWellFormed verified the bitIdentical branch (117.43-01) but never verified the notBitIdentical branch: a claim that the artifacts DIFFER, recorded with byte-identical digests on both rebuilds, was reported isWellFormed == true, BuildProvenanceEvidence.evaluate returned pass, and the 117.43 gate reported the provenance output as pass. Exact mirror of 117.43-01 in the opposite direction: there an unverified false identity claim, here an unverified false difference claim. Fix: notBitIdentical now requires at least one recorded digest that actually differs, otherwise isWellFormed == false (minimal fail-closed guard before the pre-existing limits documentation check). Commit 0ce8c5f.

117.43-07 recorded 2026-10-03 run 5 but never appended to this list (state bookkeeping gap found and repaired in run 6; the fix itself was committed in fb12fde): _evaluateShippedProvenance INFERRED the provenance verdict instead of reading it (`comparison['verdict'] == 'BIT_IDENTICAL' ? bitIdentical : notBitIdentical`), so an absent, null or misspelled verdict was silently coerced into a measured notBitIdentical claim. The gate printed provenance as pass for a manifest that stated no verdict at all. Fixed with a closed vocabulary: any value outside the two canonical strings returns null, leaving measureProvenance unmet instead of fabricating a claim.

117.43-08 the per-artifact partition was never read by anything in lib/ or test/ and ArtifactComparison had no field to hold it, so the shipped manifest's far sharper claim ("these four binaries differ, these two upstream DLLs are identical") was never measured. Proven before the fix: a manifest naming a.exe differing and b.dll identical while the recorded digests prove the exact reverse reported status=pass printing NOT_BIT_IDENTICAL - every individual claim false, only the aggregate accidentally true, because the 117.43-06 “at least one difference” rule was still satisfied. Each named artifact is now measured against its own digest and the two lists must classify the whole recorded inventory; undecodable field types and half-declared partitions fail closed, while absence of both fields stays non-claiming per 117.43-07. Commit d29f61d.

117.43-09 the rebuild WINDOWS were never read by anything in lib/ or test/ (grep for started_at/finished_at/duration_seconds returned zero matches; duration_seconds was not even parsed) and RebuildResult declared startedAt/finishedAt that nothing read, so the manifest's method claim - two INDEPENDENT clean rebuild cycles - was never measured. Proven before the fix: four impossible histories all reported status=pass with text indistinguishable from the honest case (rebuild_b starting inside rebuild_a's window; a rebuild finishing before it started; a duration_seconds contradicting its own timestamps; an unparseable timestamp). Fixed at both ends, because a domain-only fix would be theatre: the parser dropped all three fields, so every record would arrive with a null window and be waved through as a non-claim. _decodeWindow now returns null for a present-but-undecodable field so _rebuildFrom fails closed, RebuildResult.hasWellFormedWindow reads the window (both ends must parse, finish must be strictly after start), and _windowsAreIndependent additionally requires the two windows not to overlap - overlapping clean rebuilds share one build/ directory, so their digests prove nothing. Absence of BOTH ends stays non-claiming per 117.43-07 (which keeps the 117.43-06/-07 fixtures green); half-recorded is NOT absence and fails closed (the first implementation read one missing end as non-claiming and the official test caught it: Expected false, Actual true). Mistyped window fields are refused, not cast past, via the _kUndecodable sentinel. The shipped manifest still passes because its windows are genuinely honest - measured independently in this run: rebuild_a 13:27:45->13:29:47 = 122s matching its recorded duration, rebuild_b 13:30:17->13:32:12 = 115s also matching, 30s apart, both log files present. A second test moves rebuild_b's window inside rebuild_a's on the REAL shipped document with every digest, verdict and partition untouched, and must fail; if only digests were measured it would still pass. Commit be01156.

117.43-10 found and fixed in this slice (2026-10-03): the shipped comparison method claims 'SHA-256 after two INDEPENDENT CLEAN rebuild CYCLES' and 117.43-09 measured 'independent' (windows must not overlap) but NOTHING measured 'clean', because _rebuildFrom dropped 'command' and 'log' exactly as it had dropped the window fields, and RebuildResult never declared them - zero readers in lib/. Proven before the fix with a probe whose manifest was honest in every other respect: four impossible claims all reported pass - a command naming no clean step; two rebuilds run in different build modes (--release vs --debug), i.e. two different experiments compared; a log pointing at a file that does not exist; and both fields present but of the wrong type (int). Absent fields stayed a correct non-claim, which is what keeps 117.43-06/-07 fixtures green. Fix, both ends: the gate decodes 'command' and 'log' under the 117.43-09 rule (present-but-undecodable fails closed via the _kUndecodable sentinel, absent stays a non-claim) and a recorded log must resolve on disk; RebuildResult.hasWellFormedMethod requires a recorded command to name a clean step, and ranSameExperimentAs requires both rebuilds to have run the same experiment compared on a normalized form so cosmetic differences do not refuse honest manifests. The shipped manifest is unaffected because its claim is honest - measured this run, both commands carry flutter clean, both build windows --release, both logs exist on disk. RED->GREEN: 5 of 7 new tests fail before the gate change, 7/7 after, file total 75/75 (up from 68/68). Necessity proven by reverting ONLY the gate file while the domain keeps the new getters: exactly 5 named tests fail, no compile error. EOL PITFALL RECORDED: the commit warned CRLF will be replaced by LF; 3-side sha verification MUST normalize EOL first (git check-attr text=auto eol=lf), disk had 1144 CRLF vs committed 0 and only matched after normalization.

117.43-11 found and fixed in this slice (2026-10-03): build_inputs and dependency_lock exist to record WHICH file was hashed and WHAT it hashed to, as '<path> sha256 <64 hex>', and nothing ever parsed them - _hasContent only asked whether each entry was non-blank, so a fabricated 64-hex digest, an 8-character truncation, 63 or 65 hex characters, and the literal NOT-A-DIGEST all reported pass while the gate printed 'build_inputs: 5 item' as though the content had been read. Proven before the fix with eleven cases, ten of which passed; the one that failed failed for being blank rather than for its digest. The rule matches the CLAIM rather than one spelling of it (sha256/SHA256/sha-256) and deliberately stops at form: build_inputs pins digests at the provenance anchor revision 30dda0c3389a8bd9e3cae705abd51eaecbca2630, not at HEAD, so re-hashing against the live checkout would refuse an honest manifest - this repo's pubspec.yaml digest matches its CRLF variant at that revision and not the LF bytes on disk, measured across a four-variant EOL sweep after the drift hypothesis was disproved. A line that merely names the algorithm without a value states no claim and is left alone, per the non-claim rule 117.43-07 established for the comparison verdict.",

117.43-12 found and fixed in this slice (2026-10-03): the same three evidence groups were read through '(evidence[key] as List<dynamic>?)?.cast<String>()', which asserts rather than checks - a group holding [42], holding a Map, not being a list at all, or containing a blank string did not report unmet but threw a TypeError out of the gate, so a malformed manifest escaped the verdict entirely instead of failing closed. Probed before the fix: every shape printed status=NO-STATUS thrown=TypeError. Every other decode in that file was written for this under 117.43-08/-09/-10; this one was missed. A gate that crashes on malformed input is not fail-closed, which is why this is filed beside the digest rule rather than folded into it: one reads content, the other decodes shape. Now decoded by explicit _stringList, which returns null for a present-but-malformed group so the callers report unmet.",

117.43-14 found and fixed in this slice (2026-10-03): _evaluateShippedProvenance read rebuildList[0] and rebuildList[1] out of a list that may hold more, then reported the count of the two it had read as though it were the document's. Every rule added by 117.43-08/-09/-10/-12/-13 (the window, the independence of the windows, the clean command, the digest, the exit code, the reachable log, the partition) was therefore applied to two records and to no other, so a manifest recording three or more rebuilds had all but two of them never decoded and never measured. Proven before the fix by APPENDING one record to the shipped manifest, so that only the appended defect could decide the outcome: eight defects travelled in that third record (non-zero exit code, fabricated digest, window ending before it starts, command admitting no clean step, log nobody can open, duplicate label, an artifact the partition never names, and a window overlapping the first rebuild) and all eight returned pass, each reporting 'rebuild_results: 2 item' for a document recording three. 117.43-13 is this same omission seen from inside one record - it made a mistyped THIRD record fail closed, which it could not and could not have done, because the third record was never decoded. Now decodes every record, refuses two records sharing a label, holds every record to the window, method, digest, exit-code and reachable-log rules, requires every PAIR of windows to stand clear (new helper _windowsArePairwiseIndependent, since _windowsAreIndependent compares only two), and requires the partition to account for the inventory across ALL recorded rebuilds rather than the first rebuild alone. A manifest recording one rebuild stays unevaluable (the claim needs two) and one recording three is checked three times over; absent fields stay null (117.43-07) and a present-but-unreadable value stays unevaluable, hence unmet.
